name: @satsuma/lsp
description: Satsuma Language Server — standalone LSP for the Satsuma data mapping language
//files: Declares the tarball contents explicitly, which `files` lets take precedence
over every ignore file. Necessary since the tooling packages became npm
workspaces (ADR-049): npm-packlist then resolves ignore rules from the
*workspace root*, so the repo-wide .gitignore's '**/*.wasm' stripped both WASM
assets out of the tarball — reintroducing exactly the sl-vwpr breakage (a
tarball that installs cleanly and then fails every initialize request).
scripts/verify-pack.js is what caught it and what keeps it caught.
This list reproduces the pre-workspaces contents.

scripts.prebuild: npm --prefix ../satsuma-core run build && npm --prefix ../satsuma-viz-backend run build && node scripts/copy-assets.js
scripts.pretest: npm --prefix ../satsuma-core run build && npm --prefix ../satsuma-viz-backend run build && tsc && npm run test:typecheck

//dependencies: The @satsuma/* workspace packages are devDependencies, not dependencies:
dist/server.js is a self-contained esbuild bundle that inlines them, so they
are build inputs and the published tarball needs nothing from them at runtime.
They are also private and unpublishable, so declaring them as dependencies
makes `npm install -g satsuma-lsp.tgz` try to fetch @satsuma/core from the
registry and fail with a 404 (feature 42, R2 — the old `file:../` specs hid
this because npm skips an unresolvable relative file: spec). verify-pack.js
now asserts no unpublishable dependency reaches the tarball.
